```
   646→def test_high_impact_subjective_before_low_impact_mechanical():
   647→    """A subjective dimension with high headroom sorts before a mechanical
   648→    issue in a near-perfect dimension."""
   649→    from desloppify.engine._work_queue.ranking import enrich_with_impact, item_sort_key
   650→
   651→    subj_item = {
   652→        "id": "subjective::naming",
   653→        "kind": "subjective_dimension",
   654→        "detail": {"dimension_name": "Naming quality", "strict_score": 43.0},
   655→        "confidence": "medium",
   656→    }
   657→    mech_item = {
   658→        "id": "smells::src/a.py::x",
   659→        "kind": "issue",
   660→        "detector": "smells",
   661→        "confidence": "high",
   662→        "detail": {"count": 1},
   663→    }
   664→
   665→    dimension_scores = {
   666→        "Naming quality": {
   667→            "score": 43.0,
   668→            "strict": 43.0,
   669→            "failing": 3,
   670→            "detectors": {
   671→                "subjective_assessment": {"dimension_key": "naming_quality"},
   672→            },
   673→        },
   674→        "Code quality": {
   675→            "score": 97.0,
   676→            "strict": 97.0,
   677→            "checks": 200,
   678→            "failing": 1,
   679→            "detectors": {
   680→                "smells": {"weighted_failures": 1, "potential": 200},
   681→            },
   682→        },
   683→    }
   684→
   685→    enrich_with_impact([subj_item, mech_item], dimension_scores)
   686→
   687→    # Naming quality has much more headroom (57) than Code quality (3)
   688→    assert subj_item["estimated_impact"] > mech_item["estimated_impact"]
   689→    assert item_sort_key(subj_item) < item_sort_key(mech_item)
   690→
   691→
   692→def test_impact_fallback_when_no_dimension_scores():
   693→    """When no dimension_scores exist, all items get impact 0.0 and
   694→    tiebreakers provide default ordering."""
   695→    from desloppify.engine._work_queue.ranking import enrich_with_impact, item_sort_key
   696→
   697→    items = [
   698→        {
   699→            "id": "smells::src/a.py::x",
   700→            "kind": "issue",
   701→            "detector": "smells",
   702→            "confidence": "high",
   703→            "detail": {"count": 5},
   704→        },

   707→            "kind": "issue",
   708→            "detector": "smells",
   709→            "confidence": "medium",
   710→            "detail": {"count": 2},
   711→        },
   712→    ]
   713→
   714→    enrich_with_impact(items, {})
   715→
   716→    assert all(item["estimated_impact"] == 0.0 for item in items)
   717→    # High confidence sorts before medium when impact is equal
   718→    assert item_sort_key(items[0]) < item_sort_key(items[1])
```

```
   381→def test_subjective_threshold_clamped_to_valid_range():
   382→    """Threshold values outside [0, 100] are clamped, not rejected."""
   383→    state = _state(
   384→        [],

   386→            "Naming quality": {"score": 50.0, "strict": 50.0, "failing": 1, "stale": True},

   389→    # threshold=-10 clamps to 0.0 -> score 50 >= 0 -> item excluded
   390→    queue = build_work_queue(
   391→        state, count=None, include_subjective=True, subjective_threshold=-10
   392→    )
   393→    subj_items = [item for item in queue["items"] if item["kind"] == "subjective_dimension"]
   394→    assert subj_items == []
   395→
   396→    # threshold=200 clamps to 100.0 -> score 50 < 100 -> item included
   397→    queue2 = build_work_queue(
   398→        state, count=None, include_subjective=True, subjective_threshold=200
   399→    )
   400→    subj_items2 = [item for item in queue2["items"] if item["kind"] == "subjective_dimension"]
   401→    assert len(subj_items2) >= 1

   643→# ── Impact-based ordering ──────────────────────────────────
   644→
   645→
   646→def test_high_impact_subjective_before_low_impact_mechanical():
   647→    """A subjective dimension with high headroom sorts before a mechanical
   648→    issue in a near-perfect dimension."""
   649→    from desloppify.engine._work_queue.ranking import enrich_with_impact, item_sort_key
   650→
   651→    subj_item = {
   652→        "id": "subjective::naming",
   653→        "kind": "subjective_dimension",
   654→        "detail": {"dimension_name": "Naming quality", "strict_score": 43.0},
   655→        "confidence": "medium",
   656→    }
   657→    mech_item = {
   658→        "id": "smells::src/a.py::x",
   659→        "kind": "issue",
   660→        "detector": "smells",
   661→        "confidence": "high",
   662→        "detail": {"count": 1},
   663→    }
   664→
   665→    dimension_scores = {
   666→        "Naming quality": {
   667→            "score": 43.0,
   668→            "strict": 43.0,
   669→            "failing": 3,
   670→            "detectors": {
   671→                "subjective_assessment": {"dimension_key": "naming_quality"},
   672→            },
   673→        },
   674→        "Code quality": {
   675→            "score": 97.0,
   676→            "strict": 97.0,
   677→            "checks": 200,
   678→            "failing": 1,
   679→            "detectors": {
   680→                "smells": {"weighted_failures": 1, "potential": 200},
   681→            },
   682→        },
   683→    }
   684→
   685→    enrich_with_impact([subj_item, mech_item], dimension_scores)
   686→
   687→    # Naming quality has much more headroom (57) than Code quality (3)
   688→    assert subj_item["estimated_impact"] > mech_item["estimated_impact"]
   689→    assert item_sort_key(subj_item) < item_sort_key(mech_item)
   690→
   691→
   692→def test_impact_fallback_when_no_dimension_scores():
   693→    """When no dimension_scores exist, all items get impact 0.0 and
   694→    tiebreakers provide default ordering."""
   695→    from desloppify.engine._work_queue.ranking import enrich_with_impact, item_sort_key
   696→
   697→    items = [
   698→        {
   699→            "id": "smells::src/a.py::x",
   700→            "kind": "issue",
   701→            "detector": "smells",
   702→            "confidence": "high",
   703→            "detail": {"count": 5},
   704→        },
   705→        {
   706→            "id": "smells::src/b.py::y",
   707→            "kind": "issue",
   708→            "detector": "smells",
   709→            "confidence": "medium",
   710→            "detail": {"count": 2},
   711→        },
   712→    ]
   713→
   714→    enrich_with_impact(items, {})
   715→
   716→    assert all(item["estimated_impact"] == 0.0 for item in items)
   717→    # High confidence sorts before medium when impact is equal
   718→    assert item_sort_key(items[0]) < item_sort_key(items[1])

   748→    queue = build_work_queue(state, count=None, include_subjective=False)
   749→    ids = {item["id"] for item in queue["items"]}
   750→    assert "props::src/a.tsx::huge" in ids
   751→
   752→
   753→def test_detector_without_threshold_unaffected():
   754→    """Detectors without standalone_threshold (e.g. unused) pass at any confidence."""
   755→    state = _state(
   756→        [_issue("unused::src/a.py::x", detector="unused", confidence="low")]
   757→    )
   758→    queue = build_work_queue(state, count=None, include_subjective=False)
   759→    ids = {item["id"] for item in queue["items"]}
   760→    assert "unused::src/a.py::x" in ids
   761→
   762→
   763→def test_evidence_only_issue_still_in_state():
   764→    """Evidence-only issues are filtered from queue but remain in state (scoring intact)."""
   765→    issues = [_issue("props::src/a.tsx::big", detector="props", confidence="low")]
   766→    state = _state(issues)
   767→    # Issue exists in state
   768→    assert "props::src/a.tsx::big" in state["issues"]
   769→    # But not in queue
   770→    queue = build_work_queue(state, count=None, include_subjective=False)
   771→    assert len(queue["items"]) == 0
   772→
   773→
   774→def test_evidence_only_items_dont_block_subjective():
   775→    """Evidence-only items (filtered before lifecycle) don't block subjective items.
   776→
   777→    The lifecycle filter operates on the actual queue contents after all prior
   778→    filters. If evidence-only items are the only objective issues and they get
   779→    filtered out, subjective items surface because nothing objective remains.
   780→    """
   781→    # All issues are low-confidence smells (below standalone_threshold)
   782→    issues = [
   783→        _issue(f"smells::src/{c}.py::x", detector="smells", confidence="low")
   784→        for c in "abcd"
   785→    ]
   786→    state = _state(
   787→        issues,
   788→        dimension_scores={
   789→            "Naming quality": {"score": 70.0, "strict": 70.0, "failing": 1, "stale": True},
   790→        },
   791→    )
   792→
   793→    queue = build_work_queue(state, count=None, include_subjective=True)
   794→    subj_ids = [
   795→        item["id"] for item in queue["items"]
   796→        if item["kind"] == "subjective_dimension"
   797→    ]
   798→    # Evidence-only items filtered before lifecycle → no objective items remain
   799→    # → subjective items surface
   800→    assert len(subj_ids) == 1
   801→
   802→
   803→def test_low_impact_items_preserved_in_queue():
   804→    """All open issues remain in queue regardless of impact score.
   805→
   806→    The impact floor was removed — triage/skip is the authority on what matters.
   807→    """
   808→    state = _state(
   809→        [_issue("unused::src/a.py::x", detector="unused", confidence="high")],
   810→        dimension_scores={
   811→            "Code quality": {"score": 99.99, "strict": 99.99, "checks": 10000, "failing": 1},
   812→        },
   813→    )
   814→    queue = build_work_queue(state, count=None, include_subjective=False)
   815→    ids = {item["id"] for item in queue["items"]}
   816→    assert "unused::src/a.py::x" in ids
   817→
   818→

   820→    """Exactly 7 detectors have standalone_threshold='medium'."""
   821→    from desloppify.base.registry import DETECTORS
   822→
   823→    threshold_detectors = [
   824→        name for name, meta in DETECTORS.items()
   825→        if meta.standalone_threshold == "medium"
   826→    ]
   827→    assert sorted(threshold_detectors) == sorted([
   828→        "props", "patterns", "naming", "react", "smells", "dupes", "dict_keys",
   829→    ])
```

```
   487→def test_sync_import_scores_updates_metadata_on_consecutive_issues_only_import() -> None:
   488→    """A second issues_only import should update pending metadata to the latest batch."""
   489→    plan: dict = {"queue_order": []}
   490→    state: dict = {
   491→        "assessment_import_audit": [
   492→            {
   493→                "timestamp": "2026-03-10T10:00:00+00:00",
   494→                "mode": "issues_only",
   495→                "import_file": "/tmp/review-v1.json",
   496→            },
   497→        ]
   498→    }
   499→
   500→    # First issues_only import injects the workflow item with v1 metadata
   501→    r1 = sync_workflow_mod.sync_import_scores_needed(
   502→        plan,
   503→        state,
   504→        assessment_mode="issues_only",
   505→        import_file="/tmp/review-v1.json",
   506→        import_payload={
   507→            "issues": [{"id": "a"}],
   508→            "assessments": {"naming_quality": 80},
   509→            "provenance": {"packet_sha256": "hash-v1"},
   510→        },
   511→    )
   512→    assert r1.injected == ["workflow::import-scores"]
   513→    assert plan["refresh_state"]["pending_import_scores"]["packet_sha256"] == "hash-v1"
   514→
   515→    # Second issues_only import with updated data should update metadata
   516→    state["assessment_import_audit"].append(
   517→        {
   518→            "timestamp": "2026-03-10T10:10:00+00:00",
   519→            "mode": "issues_only",
   520→            "import_file": "/tmp/review-v2.json",
   521→        },
   522→    )
   523→    r2 = sync_workflow_mod.sync_import_scores_needed(
   524→        plan,
   525→        state,
   526→        assessment_mode="issues_only",
   527→        import_file="/tmp/review-v2.json",
   528→        import_payload={
   529→            "issues": [{"id": "a"}, {"id": "b"}],
   530→            "assessments": {"naming_quality": 85, "design_coherence": 70},
   531→            "provenance": {"packet_sha256": "hash-v2"},
   532→        },
   533→    )
   534→    assert r2.changes == 1
   535→    assert r2.injected == []  # not re-injected, just updated
```

```
1→"""Lightweight integrity helpers for subjective/review scoring.
     2→
     3→This module intentionally lives outside ``desloppify.intelligence.review`` so command/state
     4→paths can import it without loading the heavier review package.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→from __future__ import annotations
     8→
     9→from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping
    10→
    11→from desloppify.engine._scoring.policy.core import (
    12→    SUBJECTIVE_TARGET_MATCH_TOLERANCE,
    13→    matches_target_score,
    14→)
    15→
    16→__all__ = [
    17→    "SUBJECTIVE_TARGET_MATCH_TOLERANCE",
    18→    "is_holistic_subjective_issue",
    19→    "is_subjective_review_open",
    20→    "matches_target_score",
    21→    "subjective_review_open_breakdown",
    22→    "unassessed_subjective_dimensions",
    23→]
    24→
    25→
    26→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    27→# Internal iteration helper
    28→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    29→
    30→
    31→def _iter_issues(
    32→    issues: Mapping[str, dict] | Iterable[dict],
    33→) -> Iterable[tuple[str, dict]]:
    34→    """Yield (issue_id, issue) pairs from mapping or iterable inputs."""
    35→    if isinstance(issues, Mapping):
    36→        for issue_id, issue in issues.items():
    37→            if isinstance(issue, dict):
    38→                yield str(issue_id), issue
    39→        return
    40→
    41→    for index, issue in enumerate(issues):
    42→        if isinstance(issue, dict):
    43→            yield str(index), issue
    44→
    45→
    46→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    47→# Public helpers (formerly in integrity/review.py)
    48→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    49→
    50→
    51→def is_subjective_review_open(issue: dict) -> bool:
    52→    """Return True when a issue is an open subjective-review signal."""
    53→    return (
    54→        issue.get("status") == "open"
    55→        and issue.get("detector") == "subjective_review"
    56→    )
    57→
    58→
    59→def is_holistic_subjective_issue(issue: dict, *, issue_id: str = "") -> bool:
    60→    """Best-effort check for holistic subjective-review coverage issues.
    61→
    62→    With dimension-level subjective_review issues, this checks for legacy
    63→    holistic markers (backward compat) and the new dimension-level format.
    64→    """
    65→    candidate_id = str(issue.get("id") or issue_id or "")
    66→    # Legacy holistic markers
    67→    if "::holistic_unreviewed" in candidate_id or "::holistic_stale" in candidate_id:
    68→        return True
    69→
    70→    summary = str(issue.get("summary", "") or "").lower()
    71→    if "holistic" in summary and "review" in summary:
    72→        return True
    73→
    74→    detail = issue.get("detail", {})
    75→    if detail.get("holistic"):
    76→        return True
    77→
    78→    # Dimension-level issues are codebase-wide by nature
    79→    if issue.get("detector") == "subjective_review" and detail.get("dimension"):
    80→        return True
    81→
    82→    return False
```

```
    33→) -> Iterable[tuple[str, dict]]:
    34→    """Yield (issue_id, issue) pairs from mapping or iterable inputs."""

    36→        for issue_id, issue in issues.items():
    37→            if isinstance(issue, dict):
    38→                yield str(issue_id), issue
    39→        return
    40→
    41→    for index, issue in enumerate(issues):
    42→        if isinstance(issue, dict):

    51→def is_subjective_review_open(issue: dict) -> bool:
    52→    """Return True when a issue is an open subjective-review signal."""

    55→        and issue.get("detector") == "subjective_review"
```

```
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→from typing import Any

     8→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import StateModel, utc_now

    11→from desloppify.intelligence.review.selection import hash_file
    12→
    13→
    14→def update_reviewed_file_cache(
    15→    state: StateModel,
    16→    reviewed_files: list[str],
    17→    *,
    18→    project_root: Path | str | None = None,
    19→    utc_now_fn=utc_now,
    20→) -> None:
    21→    """Refresh per-file review cache entries from holistic payload metadata."""
    22→    refresh_review_file_cache(
    23→        state,
    24→        reviewed_files=reviewed_files,
    25→        issues_by_file=None,
    26→        project_root=project_root,
    27→        hash_file_fn=hash_file,
    28→        utc_now_fn=utc_now_fn,
    29→    )
    30→
    31→
    32→def _resolve_total_files(state: StateModel, lang_name: str | None) -> int:
    33→    """Best-effort total file count from codebase_metrics or review cache."""
    34→    review_cache = state.get("review_cache", {})
    35→    fallback = len(review_cache.get("files", {}))
    36→
    37→    codebase_metrics: object = state.get("codebase_metrics", {})
    38→    if not isinstance(codebase_metrics, dict):
    39→        return fallback
    40→
    41→    sources = []
    42→    if lang_name:
    43→        lang_metrics = codebase_metrics.get(lang_name)
    44→        if isinstance(lang_metrics, dict):
    45→            sources.append(lang_metrics)
    46→    sources.append(codebase_metrics)
    47→
    48→    for source in sources:
    49→        metric_total = source.get("total_files")
    50→        if isinstance(metric_total, int) and metric_total > 0:
    51→            return metric_total
    52→
    53→    return fallback
    54→
    55→
    56→def update_holistic_review_cache(
    57→    state: StateModel,
    58→    issues_data: list[dict],
    59→    *,
    60→    lang_name: str | None = None,
    61→    review_scope: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    62→    utc_now_fn=utc_now,
    63→) -> None:
    64→    """Store holistic review metadata in review_cache."""
    65→    review_cache = state.setdefault("review_cache", {})
    66→    now = utc_now_fn()
    67→    _, holistic_prompts, _ = load_dimensions_for_lang(lang_name or "")
    68→
    69→    valid = [
    70→        issue
    71→        for issue in issues_data
    72→        if all(key in issue for key in ("dimension", "identifier", "summary", "confidence"))
    73→        and issue["dimension"] in holistic_prompts
    74→    ]
    75→
    76→    total_override = review_scope.get("total_files") if isinstance(review_scope, dict) else None
    77→    if (
    78→        isinstance(total_override, int)
    79→        and not isinstance(total_override, bool)
    80→        and total_override > 0
    81→    ):
    82→        resolved_total_files = total_override
    83→    else:
    84→        resolved_total_files = _resolve_total_files(state, lang_name)
    85→
    86→    holistic_entry: dict[str, Any] = {
    87→        "reviewed_at": now,
    88→        "file_count_at_review": resolved_total_files,
    89→        "issue_count": len(valid),
    90→    }
    91→    if isinstance(review_scope, dict):
    92→        reviewed_files_count = review_scope.get("reviewed_files_count")
    93→        if (
    94→            isinstance(reviewed_files_count, int)
    95→            and not isinstance(reviewed_files_count, bool)
    96→            and reviewed_files_count >= 0
    97→        ):
    98→            holistic_entry["reviewed_files_count"] = reviewed_files_count
    99→        full_sweep_included = review_scope.get("full_sweep_included")
   100→        if isinstance(full_sweep_included, bool):
   101→            holistic_entry["full_sweep_included"] = full_sweep_included
   102→
   103→    review_cache["holistic"] = holistic_entry
   104→
   105→
   106→def _assessed_dimension_keys(state: StateModel) -> set[str]:
   107→    """Return dimension keys that have real (non-placeholder) assessments."""
   108→    assessments = state.get("subjective_assessments", {})
   109→    if not isinstance(assessments, dict):
   110→        return set()
   111→    keys: set[str] = set()
   112→    for dim_key, payload in assessments.items():
   113→        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
   114→            continue
   115→        if payload.get("placeholder") is True:
   116→            continue
   117→        if payload.get("source") == "scan_reset_subjective":
   118→            continue
   119→        if payload.get("reset_by") == "scan_reset_subjective":
   120→            continue
   121→        keys.add(str(dim_key))
   122→    return keys
   123→
   124→
   125→def resolve_holistic_coverage_issues(
   126→    state: StateModel,
   127→    diff: dict[str, Any],
   128→    *,
   129→    utc_now_fn=utc_now,
   130→) -> None:
   131→    """Resolve dimension-level subjective_review issues covered by import."""
   132→    assessed = _assessed_dimension_keys(state)
   133→    if not assessed:
   134→        return
   135→    now = utc_now_fn()
   136→    for issue in state.get("issues", {}).values():
   137→        if issue.get("status") != "open":
   138→            continue
   139→        if issue.get("detector") != "subjective_review":
   140→            continue
   141→        dim_key = (issue.get("detail") or {}).get("dimension", "")
   142→        if dim_key not in assessed:
   143→            continue
   144→        issue["status"] = "auto_resolved"
   145→        issue["resolved_at"] = now
   146→        issue["note"] = "resolved by review import"
   147→        issue["resolution_attestation"] = {
   148→            "kind": "agent_import",
   149→            "text": "Dimension assessment imported; coverage marker superseded",
   150→            "attested_at": now,
   151→            "scan_verified": False,
   152→        }
   153→        diff["auto_resolved"] += 1
   154→
   155→
   156→def resolve_reviewed_file_coverage_issues(
   157→    state: StateModel,
   158→    diff: dict[str, Any],
   159→    reviewed_files: list[str],
   160→    *,
   161→    utc_now_fn=utc_now,
   162→) -> None:
   163→    """No-op — per-file coverage issues no longer exist.
   164→
   165→    Kept for backward compatibility with callers that still invoke this.
   166→    """
   167→
   168→
   169→__all__ = [
   170→    "resolve_holistic_coverage_issues",
   171→    "resolve_reviewed_file_coverage_issues",
   172→    "update_holistic_review_cache",
   173→    "update_reviewed_file_cache",
   174→]
   175→
```

```
     8→from desloppify.engine._scoring.results.core import get_dimension_for_detector
     9→from desloppify.intelligence.narrative._constants import DETECTOR_TOOLS
    10→from desloppify.intelligence.narrative.action_models import ActionItem

    13→def _dimension_name(detector: str) -> str:
    14→    """Resolve user-facing dimension name for a detector."""
    15→    dimension = get_dimension_for_detector(detector)
    16→    return dimension.name if dimension else "Unknown"
    17→
    18→
    19→def _append_reorganize_actions(
    20→    actions: list[ActionItem],
    21→    by_detector: dict[str, int],
    22→    impact_for: Callable[[str, int], float],
    23→) -> None:
    24→    """Append structure/move oriented actions."""
    25→    for detector, tool_info in DETECTOR_TOOLS.items():
    26→        if tool_info["action_type"] != "reorganize":
    27→            continue
    28→        count = by_detector.get(detector, 0)

    34→            {

    36→                "detector": detector,
    37→                "count": count,
    38→                "description": f"{count} {detector} issues — {guidance}",
    39→                "command": f"desloppify show {detector} --status open",
    40→                "impact": round(impact_for(detector, count), 1),
    41→                "dimension": _dimension_name(detector),
```

```
    43→            "issue_count": 5,
    44→        }
    45→        if confirmed:
    46→            stages[name]["confirmed_at"] = "2025-06-01T00:01:00Z"
    47→            stages[name]["confirmed_text"] = "I have thoroughly reviewed all the issues in this stage"
    48→    return plan
    49→
    50→
```

```
   258→class TestFormatStrictTargetProgress:
   259→    def test_none_input(self):
   260→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress(None)
   261→        assert lines == []
   262→        assert target is None
   263→        assert gap is None
   264→
   265→    def test_non_dict_input(self):
   266→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress("not a dict")
   267→        assert lines == []
   268→        assert target is None
   269→        assert gap is None
   270→
   271→    def test_warning_only(self):
   272→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress(
   273→            {"warning": "Low data confidence"}
   274→        )
   275→        assert len(lines) == 1
   276→        assert "Low data confidence" in lines[0][0]
   277→        assert lines[0][1] == "yellow"
   278→        assert target is None
   279→
   280→    def test_target_without_current(self):
   281→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress(
   282→            {"target": 80.0}
   283→        )
   284→        assert target == 80.0
   285→        assert gap is None
   286→        assert any("unavailable" in line for line, _ in lines)
   287→
   288→    def test_below_target(self):
   289→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress(
   290→            {"target": 80.0, "current": 70.0, "gap": 10.0, "state": "below"}
   291→        )
   292→        assert target == 80.0
   293→        assert gap == 10.0
   294→        assert any("below target" in line for line, _ in lines)
   295→        assert any(color == "yellow" for _, color in lines)
   296→
   297→    def test_above_target(self):
   298→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress(
   299→            {"target": 80.0, "current": 90.0, "gap": -10.0, "state": "above"}
   300→        )
   301→        assert target == 80.0
   302→        assert gap == -10.0
   303→        assert any("above target" in line for line, _ in lines)
   304→        assert any(color == "green" for _, color in lines)
   305→
   306→    def test_on_target(self):
   307→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress(
   308→            {"target": 80.0, "current": 80.0, "gap": 0.0, "state": "on"}
   309→        )
   310→        assert target == 80.0
   311→        assert gap == 0.0
   312→        assert any("on target" in line for line, _ in lines)
   313→
   314→    def test_gap_computed_when_missing(self):
   315→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress(
   316→            {"target": 80.0, "current": 70.0, "state": "below"}
   317→        )
   318→        assert gap == 10.0
   319→
   320→    def test_warning_plus_below(self):
   321→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress(
   322→            {"target": 80.0, "current": 70.0, "gap": 10.0, "state": "below", "warning": "Low confidence"}
   323→        )
   324→        assert len(lines) == 2
   325→        assert "Low confidence" in lines[0][0]
   326→        assert "below target" in lines[1][0]
   327→
   328→    def test_integer_target(self):
   329→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress(
   330→            {"target": 80, "current": 75, "gap": 5, "state": "below"}
   331→        )
   332→        assert target == 80.0
   333→        assert isinstance(target, float)
```

```
   253→from desloppify.app.commands.status.strict_target import (  # noqa: E402
   254→    format_strict_target_progress,
   255→)

   257→
   258→class TestFormatStrictTargetProgress:
   259→    def test_none_input(self):
   260→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress(None)
   261→        assert lines == []
   262→        assert target is None
   263→        assert gap is None
   264→
   265→    def test_non_dict_input(self):
   266→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress("not a dict")
   267→        assert lines == []
   268→        assert target is None
   269→        assert gap is None
   270→
   271→    def test_warning_only(self):
   272→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress(
   273→            {"warning": "Low data confidence"}
   274→        )
   275→        assert len(lines) == 1
   276→        assert "Low data confidence" in lines[0][0]
   277→        assert lines[0][1] == "yellow"
   278→        assert target is None
   279→
   280→    def test_target_without_current(self):
   281→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress(
   282→            {"target": 80.0}
   283→        )
   284→        assert target == 80.0
   285→        assert gap is None
   286→        assert any("unavailable" in line for line, _ in lines)
   287→
   288→    def test_below_target(self):
   289→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress(
   290→            {"target": 80.0, "current": 70.0, "gap": 10.0, "state": "below"}
   291→        )
   292→        assert target == 80.0
   293→        assert gap == 10.0
   294→        assert any("below target" in line for line, _ in lines)
   295→        assert any(color == "yellow" for _, color in lines)
   296→
   297→    def test_above_target(self):
   298→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress(
   299→            {"target": 80.0, "current": 90.0, "gap": -10.0, "state": "above"}
   300→        )
   301→        assert target == 80.0
   302→        assert gap == -10.0
   303→        assert any("above target" in line for line, _ in lines)
   304→        assert any(color == "green" for _, color in lines)
   305→
   306→    def test_on_target(self):
   307→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress(
   308→            {"target": 80.0, "current": 80.0, "gap": 0.0, "state": "on"}
   309→        )
   310→        assert target == 80.0
   311→        assert gap == 0.0
   312→        assert any("on target" in line for line, _ in lines)
   313→
   314→    def test_gap_computed_when_missing(self):
   315→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress(
   316→            {"target": 80.0, "current": 70.0, "state": "below"}
   317→        )
   318→        assert gap == 10.0
   319→
   320→    def test_warning_plus_below(self):
   321→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress(
   322→            {"target": 80.0, "current": 70.0, "gap": 10.0, "state": "below", "warning": "Low confidence"}
   323→        )
   324→        assert len(lines) == 2
   325→        assert "Low confidence" in lines[0][0]
   326→        assert "below target" in lines[1][0]
   327→
   328→    def test_integer_target(self):
   329→        lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress(
   330→            {"target": 80, "current": 75, "gap": 5, "state": "below"}
   331→        )
   332→        assert target == 80.0
   333→        assert isinstance(target, float)
   334→

   376→class TestPrintFixFileSample:

   380→        test_file = tmp_path / "test.py"

   382→        filepath = str(test_file)
   383→        result = {"file": filepath, "removed": ["var_a"]}
   384→        entries = [{"file": filepath, "name": "var_a", "line": 3}]

   390→    @patch("desloppify.app.commands.autofix.preview.colorize", side_effect=lambda t, _c: t)

   392→    def test_handles_missing_file(self, _mock_rel, _mock_colorize, capsys):

   394→        entries = [{"file": "/nonexistent/path.py", "name": "x", "line": 1}]
   395→        _print_fix_file_sample(result, entries)
   396→        # Should not crash, just return silently
   397→        assert capsys.readouterr().out == ""

   399→    @patch("desloppify.app.commands.autofix.preview.colorize", side_effect=lambda t, _c: t)

   401→    def test_caps_at_2_entries_per_file(self, _mock_rel, _mock_colorize, capsys, tmp_path):
   402→        test_file = tmp_path / "test.py"
   403→        test_file.write_text("a\nb\nc\nd\ne\nf\ng\nh\ni\nj\n")
   404→        filepath = str(test_file)
   405→        result = {"file": filepath, "removed": ["v1", "v2", "v3"]}
   406→        entries = [
   407→            {"file": filepath, "name": "v1", "line": 2},
   408→            {"file": filepath, "name": "v2", "line": 5},
   409→            {"file": filepath, "name": "v3", "line": 8},
   410→        ]
   411→        _print_fix_file_sample(result, entries)
   412→        out = capsys.readouterr().out
   413→        # Should show v1 and v2, not v3 (capped at 2)
   414→        assert "v1" in out
   415→        assert "v2" in out
   416→        assert "v3" not in out
```

```
    21→def _print_resolve_summary(*, status: str, all_resolved: list[str]) -> None:
    22→    verb = "Reopened" if status == "open" else "Resolved"
    23→    print(colorize(f"\n{verb} {len(all_resolved)} issue(s) as {status}:", "green"))

    25→        print(f"  {fid}")
    26→    if len(all_resolved) > 20:

    29→
    30→def _print_wontfix_batch_warning(
    31→    state: dict,
    32→    *,
    33→    status: str,
    34→    resolved_count: int,
    35→) -> None:
    36→    if status != "wontfix" or resolved_count <= 10:
    37→        return
    38→    wontfix_count = sum(
    39→        1 for issue in state["issues"].values() if issue["status"] == "wontfix"
    40→    )
    41→    actionable = sum(
    42→        1
    43→        for issue in state["issues"].values()
    44→        if issue["status"]
    45→        in ("open", "wontfix", "fixed", "auto_resolved", "false_positive")
    46→    )
    47→    wontfix_pct = round(wontfix_count / actionable * 100) if actionable else 0
    48→    print(
    49→        colorize(
    50→            f"\n  ⚠ Wontfix debt is now {wontfix_count} issues ({wontfix_pct}% of actionable).",
    51→            "yellow",
    52→        )
    53→    )
    54→    print(
    55→        colorize(
    56→            '    The strict score reflects this. Run `desloppify show "*" --status wontfix` to review.',
    57→            "dim",
    58→        )
    59→    )
    60→
    61→
    62→def _delta_suffix(delta: float) -> str:
    63→    if abs(delta) < 0.05:
    64→        return ""
    65→    return f" ({'+' if delta > 0 else ''}{delta:.1f})"
    66→
    67→

    75→    state: dict,

    83→        return
    84→
    85→    overall_delta = new.overall - (prev_overall or 0)
    86→    objective_delta = new.objective - (prev_objective or 0)

    96→        + colorize(

    98→        )

   101→        print_strict_target_nudge(new.strict, target_strict, show_next=False)
   102→    print_strict_gap_note(status, overall=new.overall, strict=new.strict)
   103→    print_post_resolve_guidance(
   104→        status=status,

   106→        overall_delta=overall_delta,

   117→    has_review = any(

   119→        for fid in all_resolved

   122→        return
   123→
   124→    stale_dims = sorted(
   125→        dim
   126→        for dim in {
   127→            str(

   129→            ).strip()
   130→            for fid in all_resolved
   131→            if state["issues"].get(fid, {}).get("detector") == "review"
   132→        }
   133→        if dim and dim in (state.get("subjective_assessments") or {})
   134→    )
   135→    if not stale_dims:
   136→        return
   137→
   138→    shown = ", ".join(stale_dims[:3])
   139→    if len(stale_dims) > 3:
   140→        shown = f"{shown}, +{len(stale_dims) - 3} more"
   141→    print(
   142→        colorize(
   143→            f"  Subjective scores unchanged — re-run review for updated scores: {shown}",
   144→            "yellow",
   145→        )
   146→    )
   147→    print(
   148→        colorize(
   149→            "  Next subjective step: "
   150→            + (
   151→                "`desloppify review --prepare --dimensions "
   152→                f"{','.join(stale_dims)} --force-review-rerun`"
   153→            ),
   154→            "dim",
   155→        )
   156→    )
   157→
   158→
   159→def _render_uncommitted_block(uncommitted: list[str], just_resolved: list[str]) -> None:
   160→    """Print the uncommitted issues section."""
   161→    count = len(uncommitted)
   162→    just_set = set(just_resolved)
   163→    print(f"\n  Uncommitted work ({count} resolved issue{'s' if count != 1 else ''}):")
   164→    for fid in uncommitted[:5]:
   165→        marker = colorize("●", "green") if fid in just_set else "○"
   166→        tag = "  (just now)" if fid in just_set else ""
   167→        print(f"    {marker} {fid}{tag}")
   168→    if count > 5:
   169→        print(f"    ... and {count - 5} more")
   170→
   171→
   172→def _render_committed_block(commit_log: list[dict]) -> None:
   173→    """Print the already-committed section (last 3 commits)."""
   174→    if not commit_log:
   175→        return
   176→    committed_count = sum(len(r.get("issue_ids", [])) for r in commit_log)
   177→    nc = len(commit_log)
   178→    print(f"\n  Already committed ({nc} commit{'s' if nc != 1 else ''}, {committed_count} issue{'s' if committed_count != 1 else ''}):")
   179→    for record in commit_log[-3:]:
   180→        sha = record.get("sha", "?")[:7]
   181→        note = record.get("note", "")
   182→        fc = len(record.get("issue_ids", []))
   183→        note_str = f' — "{note}"' if note else ""
   184→        print(f"    {sha}{note_str} ({fc} issue{'s' if fc != 1 else ''})")
   185→
   186→
   187→def render_commit_guidance(
   188→    state: dict,
   189→    plan: dict | None,
   190→    just_resolved: list[str],
   191→    status: str,
   192→) -> None:
   193→    """Show commit tracking guidance after a resolve."""
   194→    if status != "fixed" or plan is None:
   195→        return
   196→
   197→    try:
   198→        config = load_config()
   199→        if not config.get("commit_tracking_enabled", True):
   200→            return
   201→
   202→        git = detect_git_context()
   203→        if not git.available:
   204→            return
   205→
   206→        uncommitted = get_uncommitted_issues(plan)
   207→        if not uncommitted:
   208→            return
   209→
   210→        pr_number = config.get("commit_pr", 0)
   211→
   212→        print(colorize("\n  ── Commit Tracking ──────────────────────────", "dim"))
   213→        print(f"  Branch: {git.branch or '?'}    HEAD: {git.head_sha or '?'}")
   214→        if pr_number:
   215→            print(f"  PR: #{pr_number}")
   216→
   217→        _render_uncommitted_block(uncommitted, just_resolved)
   218→        _render_committed_block(plan.get("commit_log", []))
   219→
   220→        template = config.get(
   221→            "commit_message_template",
   222→            "desloppify: {status} {count} issue(s) — {summary}",
   223→        )
   224→        msg = suggest_commit_message(plan, template)
   225→        if msg:
   226→            print("\n  Suggested commit message:")
   227→            print(colorize(f'    "{msg}"', "cyan"))
   228→
   229→        print(colorize("\n  After committing → `desloppify plan commit-log record`", "dim"))
   230→        print(colorize("  ─────────────────────────────────────────────", "dim"))
   231→
   232→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   233→        logging.getLogger(__name__).debug(
   234→            "commit guidance rendering skipped", exc_info=True,
   235→        )
   236→
   237→
   238→def _print_next_command(state: dict) -> str:
   239→    remaining = sum(
   240→        1
   241→        for issue in state["issues"].values()
   242→        if issue["status"] == "open"
   243→        and not issue.get("suppressed")
   244→    )
   245→    next_command = "desloppify scan"
   246→    if remaining > 0:
   247→        suffix = "s" if remaining != 1 else ""
   248→        print(
   249→            colorize(
   250→                f"\n  {remaining} issue{suffix} remaining — run `desloppify next`",
   251→                "dim",
   252→            )
   253→        )
   254→        next_command = "desloppify next"
   255→    print(colorize(f"  Next command: `{next_command}`", "dim"))
   256→    print()
   257→    return next_command
   258→
```

```
   177→    nc = len(commit_log)
   178→    print(f"\n  Already committed ({nc} commit{'s' if nc != 1 else ''}, {committed_count} issue{'s' if committed_count != 1 else ''}):")
   179→    for record in commit_log[-3:]:
   180→        sha = record.get("sha", "?")[:7]
   181→        note = record.get("note", "")
   182→        fc = len(record.get("issue_ids", []))
   183→        note_str = f' — "{note}"' if note else ""
   184→        print(f"    {sha}{note_str} ({fc} issue{'s' if fc != 1 else ''})")
   185→
   186→
   187→def render_commit_guidance(
   188→    state: dict,
   189→    plan: dict | None,
   190→    just_resolved: list[str],
   191→    status: str,
   192→) -> None:
   193→    """Show commit tracking guidance after a resolve."""
   194→    if status != "fixed" or plan is None:
   195→        return
   196→
   197→    try:
   198→        config = load_config()
   199→        if not config.get("commit_tracking_enabled", True):
   200→            return
   201→
   202→        git = detect_git_context()
   203→        if not git.available:
   204→            return
   205→
   206→        uncommitted = get_uncommitted_issues(plan)
   207→        if not uncommitted:
   208→            return
   209→
   210→        pr_number = config.get("commit_pr", 0)
   211→
   212→        print(colorize("\n  ── Commit Tracking ──────────────────────────", "dim"))
   213→        print(f"  Branch: {git.branch or '?'}    HEAD: {git.head_sha or '?'}")
   214→        if pr_number:
   215→            print(f"  PR: #{pr_number}")
   216→
   217→        _render_uncommitted_block(uncommitted, just_resolved)
   218→        _render_committed_block(plan.get("commit_log", []))
   219→
   220→        template = config.get(
   221→            "commit_message_template",
   222→            "desloppify: {status} {count} issue(s) — {summary}",
   223→        )
   224→        msg = suggest_commit_message(plan, template)
   225→        if msg:
   226→            print("\n  Suggested commit message:")
   227→            print(colorize(f'    "{msg}"', "cyan"))
   228→
   229→        print(colorize("\n  After committing → `desloppify plan commit-log record`", "dim"))
   230→        print(colorize("  ─────────────────────────────────────────────", "dim"))
   231→
   232→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   233→        logging.getLogger(__name__).debug(
   234→            "commit guidance rendering skipped", exc_info=True,
   235→        )
   236→
   237→
   238→def _print_next_command(state: dict) -> str:
   239→    remaining = sum(
   240→        1
   241→        for issue in state["issues"].values()
   242→        if issue["status"] == "open"
   243→        and not issue.get("suppressed")
   244→    )
   245→    next_command = "desloppify scan"
   246→    if remaining > 0:
   247→        suffix = "s" if remaining != 1 else ""
   248→        print(
   249→            colorize(
   250→                f"\n  {remaining} issue{suffix} remaining — run `desloppify next`",
   251→                "dim",
   252→            )
   253→        )
   254→        next_command = "desloppify next"
   255→    print(colorize(f"  Next command: `{next_command}`", "dim"))
   256→    print()
   257→    return next_command
   258→
```

```
    15→def _state_with_review_issues(*ids: str) -> dict:
    16→    """Build minimal state with open review issues."""
    17→    issues = {}
    18→    for fid in ids:
    19→        issues[fid] = {
    20→            "status": "open",
    21→            "detector": "review",
    22→            "file": "test.py",
    23→            "summary": f"Review issue {fid}",
    24→            "confidence": "medium",
    25→            "tier": 2,
    26→            "detail": {"dimension": "abstraction_fitness"},
    27→        }
    28→    return {"issues": issues, "scan_count": 5, "dimension_scores": {}}
    29→
    30→
    31→def _plan_with_stages(*stage_names: str, confirmed: bool = False) -> dict:
    32→    """Build a plan with triage stages pre-recorded."""
    33→    plan = empty_plan()
    34→    plan["queue_order"] = list(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS)
    35→    meta = plan.setdefault("epic_triage_meta", {})
    36→    stages = meta.setdefault("triage_stages", {})
    37→    for name in stage_names:
    38→        stages[name] = {
    39→            "stage": name,
    40→            "report": f"A sufficiently long report for {name} stage that meets minimum length requirements and more text — covers r1 r2 r3",
    41→            "cited_ids": ["r1", "r2", "r3"],
    42→            "timestamp": "2025-06-01T00:00:00Z",
    43→            "issue_count": 5,
    44→        }
    45→        if confirmed:
    46→            stages[name]["confirmed_at"] = "2025-06-01T00:01:00Z"
    47→            stages[name]["confirmed_text"] = "I have thoroughly reviewed all the issues in this stage"
    48→    return plan
    49→
    50→
    51→def _fake_runtime(state: dict):
    52→    """Build a minimal command_runtime return."""
    53→    return type("Ctx", (), {"state": state, "config": {}})()
    54→
    55→
    56→def _fake_args(**overrides) -> argparse.Namespace:
    57→    """Build an argparse.Namespace with default triage args."""
    58→    defaults = {
    59→        "lang": None,
    60→        "path": ".",
    61→        "confirm": None,
    62→        "attestation": None,
    63→        "confirmed": None,
    64→        "stage": None,
    65→        "report": None,
    66→        "complete": False,
    67→        "confirm_existing": False,
    68→        "strategy": None,
    69→        "note": None,
    70→        "start": False,
    71→        "dry_run": False,
    72→    }
    73→    defaults.update(overrides)
    74→    return argparse.Namespace(**defaults)
```

```
    31→def _plan_with_stages(*stage_names: str, confirmed: bool = False) -> dict:
    32→    """Build a plan with triage stages pre-recorded."""

    47→            stages[name]["confirmed_text"] = "I have thoroughly reviewed all the issues in this stage"
```

```json
  "new_string": "    def test_reviewed_files_auto_resolves_per_file_coverage_markers(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"resolve_reviewed_file_coverage_issues is now a no-op.\n\n        Dimension-level resolution is handled by resolve_holistic_coverage_issues\n        which checks assessed dimensions in state.  This test verifies that\n        importing a holistic review with an assessed dimension resolves the\n        dimension-level subjective_review issue.\n        \"\"\"\n        state = empty_state()\n\n        coverage_id = \"subjective_review::.::high_level_elegance\"\n        state[\"issues\"][coverage_id] = {\n            \"id\": coverage_id,\n            \"detector\": \"subjective_review\",\n            \"file\": \".\",\n            \"name\": \"high_level_elegance\",\n            \"status\": \"open\",\n            \"summary\": \"High elegance — no assessment on record\",\n            \"detail\": {\"reason\": \"unassessed\", \"dimension\": \"high_level_elegance\"},\n            \"tier\": 4,\n            \"confidence\": \"low\",\n            \"first_seen\": \"2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00\",\n            \"last_seen\": \"2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00\",\n            \"resolved_at\": None,\n            \"reopen_count\": 0,\n            \"note\": None,\n        }\n\n        payload = {\n            \"assessments\": {\"high_level_elegance\": 95},\n            \"issues\": [],\n        }\n\n        from desloppify.base.runtime_state import RuntimeContext, runtime_scope\n\n        ctx = RuntimeContext(project_root=tmp_path)\n        with runtime_scope(ctx):\n            diff = _call_import_holistic_issues(payload, state, \"python\", project_root=tmp_path)\n\n        assert diff[\"auto_resolved\"] >= 1\n        assert state[\"issues\"][coverage_id][\"status\"] == \"auto_resolved\""
```

```
    44→            meta["triage_stages"] = {}

    47→            services.append_log_entry(
    48→                plan,
    49→                "triage_start",
    50→                actor="user",
    51→                detail={"action": "restart", "cleared_stages": list(stages.keys())},
    52→            )
    53→            services.save_plan(plan)
    54→            print(colorize("  Stages cleared. Begin with observe:", "green"))
    55→        else:
    56→            _helpers_mod.inject_triage_stages(plan)
    57→            services.save_plan(plan)
    58→            print(colorize("  Begin with observe:", "green"))
    59→        print(colorize(f"    {TRIAGE_CMD_OBSERVE}", "dim"))
    60→        return
    61→
    62→    attestation: str | None = getattr(args, "attestation", None)

    74→    if start_outcome.status == "blocked":

    79→    print(colorize("  Begin with observe:", "dim"))
    80→    print(colorize(f"    {TRIAGE_CMD_OBSERVE}", "dim"))

    83→def _run_staged_runner(

    98→        run_codex_pipeline(

   114→    prompt = services.build_triage_prompt(si)

   116→    print(colorize("  Cluster triage - dry run", "bold"))

   121→    print(f"  Resolved since last: {len(si.resolved_since_last)}")
   122→    print(colorize("\n  Prompt that would be sent to LLM:", "dim"))
   123→    print()
   124→    print(prompt)
   125→
   126→
   127→def run_triage_workflow(
   128→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   129→    *,
   130→    services: TriageServices,
   131→    require_issue_inventory_fn: Callable[[dict], bool],
   132→) -> None:
   133→    """Route `plan triage` args through one orchestration seam."""
   134→    runtime = services.command_runtime(args)
   135→    state = runtime.state
   136→    if not require_issue_inventory_fn(state):
   137→        return
   138→
   139→    if getattr(args, "stage_prompt", None):
   140→        cmd_stage_prompt(args, services=services)
   141→        return
   142→    if getattr(args, "run_stages", False):
   143→        _run_staged_runner(args, services=services)
   144→        return
   145→    if getattr(args, "start", False):
   146→        _cmd_triage_start(args, state=state, services=services)
   147→        return
   148→    if getattr(args, "confirm", None):
   149→        _confirmations_router_mod.cmd_confirm_stage(args, services=services)
   150→        return
   151→    if getattr(args, "complete", False):
   152→        cmd_triage_complete(args, services=services)
   153→        return
   154→    if getattr(args, "confirm_existing", False):
   155→        cmd_confirm_existing(args, services=services)
   156→        return
   157→
   158→    stage = getattr(args, "stage", None)
   159→    if run_stage_command(stage, args, services=services):
   160→        return
   161→
   162→    if getattr(args, "dry_run", False):
   163→        _run_dry_run(services=services, state=state)
   164→        return
   165→
   166→    _display_mod.cmd_triage_dashboard(args, services=services)
   167→
   168→
   169→__all__ = ["run_triage_workflow"]
```

```
    46→            "issue_count": 5,
    47→        }
    48→        if confirmed:
    49→            stages[name]["confirmed_at"] = "2025-06-01T00:01:00Z"
    50→            stages[name]["confirmed_text"] = "I have thoroughly reviewed all the issues in this stage"
```

```
    59→class TestAutoStartTriage:
    60→    def test_observe_auto_starts_triage(self, monkeypatch, capsys):
    61→        """When no triage stages in queue, --stage observe auto-injects them."""
    62→        plan = empty_plan()
    63→        # No triage stage IDs in queue_order
    64→        assert not any(sid in plan.get("queue_order", []) for sid in TRIAGE_IDS)
    65→
    66→        state = _state_with_issues("r1", "r2", "r3", "r4", "r5")
    67→        monkeypatch.setattr(triage_mod, "load_plan", lambda *a, **kw: plan)
    68→        monkeypatch.setattr(triage_mod, "command_runtime", lambda args: _fake_runtime(state))
    69→        monkeypatch.setattr(triage_mod, "require_issue_inventory", lambda s: True)
    70→        monkeypatch.setattr(triage_mod, "save_plan", lambda p: None)
    71→

    73→            "This is a thorough analysis of the naming and architecture issues. "
    74→            "The main themes are inconsistent naming conventions across modules, "
    75→            "and some architectural coupling between components."
    76→        )
    77→        args = _fake_args(stage="observe", report=long_report)
    78→        triage_mod.cmd_plan_triage(args)
    79→

    81→        assert all(sid in plan.get("queue_order", []) for sid in TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS)
    82→        # Stage should be recorded
    83→        stages = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {}).get("triage_stages", {})
    84→        assert "observe" in stages
```

```
    70→        monkeypatch.setattr(triage_mod, "save_plan", lambda p: None)
    71→
```

```
    15→def _state_with_issues(*ids: str, dimension: str = "naming") -> dict:
    16→    issues = {}
    17→    for fid in ids:
    18→        issues[fid] = {
    19→            "status": "open",
    20→            "detector": "review",
    21→            "file": "test.py",
    22→            "summary": f"Review issue {fid}",
    23→            "confidence": "medium",
    24→            "tier": 2,
    25→            "detail": {"dimension": dimension},
    26→        }
    27→    return {"issues": issues, "scan_count": 5, "dimension_scores": {}}

    30→def _plan_with_stages(*stage_names: str, confirmed: bool = False) -> dict:
    31→    plan = empty_plan()
    32→    plan["queue_order"] = list(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS)
    33→    meta = plan.setdefault("epic_triage_meta", {})
    34→    stages = meta.setdefault("triage_stages", {})
    35→    for name in stage_names:
    36→        stages[name] = {
    37→            "stage": name,
    38→            "report": (
    39→                "A sufficiently long report for the stage that meets minimum "
    40→                "length requirements and more text to ensure validation passes"
    41→                " — covers r1 r2 r3 r4 r5"
    42→            ),
    43→            "cited_ids": ["r1", "r2", "r3"],
    44→            "timestamp": "2025-06-01T00:00:00Z",
    45→            "issue_count": 5,
    46→        }
    47→        if confirmed:
    48→            stages[name]["confirmed_at"] = "2025-06-01T00:01:00Z"
    49→            stages[name]["confirmed_text"] = (
    50→                "I have thoroughly reviewed all the issues in naming dimension "
    51→                "and this stage analysis is complete"
    52→            )
    53→    return plan

    68→        "cluster_key": "",
    69→        "action": None,
    70→    }
    71→    return plan
```

   ```python
   from desloppify.app.commands.plan.triage.services import TriageServices

   def _fake_services(plan, state, save_plan_fn=None):
       return TriageServices(
           command_runtime=lambda args: _fake_runtime(state),
           load_plan=lambda *a, **kw: plan,
           save_plan=save_plan_fn or (lambda p, *a, **kw: None),
           collect_triage_input=lambda p, s: type("TI", (), {
               "open_issues": s.get("issues", {}),
               "new_since_last": [], "resolved_since_last": [],
               "existing_clusters": {},

           detect_recurring_patterns=lambda _a, _b: {},
           append_log_entry=lambda *a, **kw: None,
           extract_issue_citations=lambda text, ids: set(),
           build_triage_prompt=lambda si: "prompt",
       )

   def _patch_triage(monkeypatch, plan, state, save_plan_fn=None):
       monkeypatch.setattr(triage_mod, "default_triage_services",
           lambda: _fake_services(plan, state, save_plan_fn))
       monkeypatch.setattr(triage_mod, "require_issue_inventory", lambda s: True)
   ```

   The fix pattern for triage tests established in `test_triage_confirmation.py` is:
   ```python
   from desloppify.app.commands.plan.triage.services import TriageServices

   def _fake_services(plan, state, save_plan_fn=None):
       return TriageServices(
           command_runtime=lambda args: _fake_runtime(state),
           load_plan=lambda *a, **kw: plan,
           save_plan=save_plan_fn or (lambda p, *a, **kw: None),
           collect_triage_input=lambda p, s: type("TI", (), {
               "open_issues": s.get("issues", {}),
               "new_since_last": [], "resolved_since_last": [],
               "existing_clusters": {},
           })(),
           detect_recurring_patterns=lambda _a, _b: {},
           append_log_entry=lambda *a, **kw: None,
           extract_issue_citations=lambda text, ids: set(),
           build_triage_prompt=lambda si: "prompt",
       )

   def _patch_triage(monkeypatch, plan, state, save_plan_fn=None):
       monkeypatch.setattr(triage_mod, "default_triage_services",
           lambda: _fake_services(plan, state, save_plan_fn))
       monkeypatch.setattr(triage_mod, "require_issue_inventory", lambda s: True)
   ```

   Then each test replaces the 3-4 monkeypatch lines with a single `_patch_triage(monkeypatch, plan, state, save_plan_fn)` call.

```
    28→
    29→def cmd_cluster_update(
    30→    args: argparse.Namespace,
    31→    *,
    32→    services: ClusterUpdateServices | None = None,
    33→    plan_lock_fn=plan_lock,
    34→) -> None:
    35→    """Update cluster description, steps, and/or priority."""
    36→    request = build_request(args)
    37→    resolved_services = services or ClusterUpdateServices(
    38→        load_plan_fn=load_plan,
    39→        save_plan_fn=save_plan,

    41→        parse_steps_file_fn=parse_steps_file,
    42→        normalize_step_fn=normalize_step,
    43→        step_summary_fn=step_summary,
    44→        utc_now_fn=utc_now,
    45→        colorize_fn=colorize,
    46→    )
    47→    if not request.has_updates():
    48→        print_no_update_warning(colorize_fn=resolved_services.colorize_fn)
    49→        return
    50→
    51→    with plan_lock_fn():
    52→        run_cluster_update_locked(request, services=resolved_services)
    53→
    54→
    55→__all__ = ["cmd_cluster_update"]
```

```
   647→def test_high_impact_subjective_before_low_impact_mechanical():
   648→    """A subjective dimension with high headroom sorts before a mechanical
   649→    issue in a near-perfect dimension."""
   650→    from desloppify.engine._work_queue.ranking import enrich_with_impact, item_sort_key
   651→
   652→    subj_item = {
   653→        "id": "subjective::naming",
   654→        "kind": "subjective_dimension",
   655→        "detail": {"dimension_name": "Naming quality", "strict_score": 43.0},
   656→        "confidence": "medium",
   657→    }
   658→    mech_item = {
   659→        "id": "smells::src/a.py::x",
   660→        "kind": "issue",
   661→        "detector": "smells",
   662→        "confidence": "high",
   663→        "detail": {"count": 1},
   664→    }
   665→
   666→    dimension_scores = {
   667→        "Naming quality": {
   668→            "score": 43.0,
   669→            "strict": 43.0,
   670→            "failing": 3,
   671→            "detectors": {
   672→                "subjective_assessment": {"dimension_key": "naming_quality"},
   673→            },
   674→        },
   675→        "Code quality": {
   676→            "score": 97.0,
   677→            "strict": 97.0,
   678→            "checks": 200,
   679→            "failing": 1,
   680→            "detectors": {
   681→                "smells": {"weighted_failures": 1, "potential": 200},
   682→            },
   683→        },
   684→    }
   685→
   686→    enrich_with_impact([subj_item, mech_item], dimension_scores)
   687→
   688→    # Naming quality has much more headroom (57) than Code quality (3)
   689→    assert subj_item["estimated_impact"] > mech_item["estimated_impact"]
   690→    assert item_sort_key(subj_item) < item_sort_key(mech_item)
```

```
   204→
   205→def _gather_subjective_items(
   206→    state: StateModel,
   207→    opts: QueueBuildOptions,
   208→    threshold: float,
   209→) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   210→    """Build subjective dimension candidates.
   211→
   212→    Lifecycle filtering (endgame gating) happens in ``apply_lifecycle_filter``,
   213→    not here. This function only handles configuration and scope.
   214→    """
   215→    if not opts.include_subjective:
   216→        return []
   217→    if opts.status not in {"open", "all"}:
   218→        return []
   219→    if opts.chronic:
   220→        return []
   221→
   222→    candidates = build_subjective_items(
   223→        state, state.get("issues", {}), threshold=threshold,
   224→    )
   225→    return [item for item in candidates if scope_matches(item, opts.scope)]
   226→
   227→
   228→def _gather_workflow_items(
   229→    state: StateModel, plan: dict | None, status: str,
   230→) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   231→    """Inject triage stages, checkpoints, and create-plan when plan is active."""
   232→    if not plan or status not in {"open", "all"}:
   233→        return []
   234→
   235→    items: list[WorkQueueItem] = []
   236→    for builder in (build_deferred_disposition_item, build_run_scan_item):
   237→        item = builder(plan)
   238→        if item is not None:
   239→            items.append(item)
   240→    items.extend(build_triage_stage_items(plan, state))
   241→    for builder in (
   242→        build_score_checkpoint_item,
   243→        build_import_scores_item,
   244→        build_communicate_score_item,
   245→    ):
   246→        item = builder(plan, state)
   247→        if item is not None:
   248→            items.append(item)
   249→    plan_item = build_create_plan_item(plan)
   250→    if plan_item is not None:
   251→        items.append(plan_item)
   252→    return items
   253→
   254→
   255→def _planned_item_ids(plan: dict) -> set[str]:
   256→    """Collect IDs explicitly tracked by the living plan."""
   257→    tracked_ids: set[str] = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   258→    tracked_ids.update(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
   259→    tracked_ids.update(plan.get("overrides", {}).keys())
```

```
104→def build_work_queue(
   105→    state: StateModel,
   106→    *,
   107→    options: QueueBuildOptions | None = None,
   108→) -> WorkQueueResult:
   109→    """Build the raw ranked work queue without execution/backlog filtering."""
   110→    return _build_work_queue_with_visibility(
   111→        state,
   112→        options=options,
   113→        visibility=QueueVisibility.ALL,
   114→    )
   115→
   116→
   117→def _build_work_queue_with_visibility(
   118→    state: StateModel,
   119→    *,
   120→    options: QueueBuildOptions | None = None,
   121→    visibility: str = QueueVisibility.ALL,
   122→) -> WorkQueueResult:
   123→    """Build a ranked work queue from state issues.
   124→
   125→    Pipeline:
   126→    1. Gather    — issue items, subjective dimensions, workflow stages
   127→    2. Score     — estimate impact from dimension headroom
   128→    3. Presort   — stamp plan positions, separate skipped items
   129→    4. Lifecycle — filter endgame-only items when objective work remains
   130→    5. Sort      — rank by impact/confidence, apply plan order
   131→    6. Limit     — truncate to count, optionally add explain metadata
   132→    """
   133→    opts = options or QueueBuildOptions()
   134→    plan, scan_path, status, threshold = _resolve_inputs(opts, state)
   135→
   136→    # 1. Gather
   137→    items = build_issue_items(
   138→        state, scan_path=scan_path, status_filter=status,
   139→        scope=opts.scope, chronic=opts.chronic,
   140→    )
   141→    items += _gather_subjective_items(state, opts, threshold)
   142→    items += _gather_workflow_items(state, plan, status)
   143→    items = _filter_plan_visibility(items, plan, visibility=visibility)
   144→
   145→    # 2. Score
   146→    enrich_with_impact(items, state.get("dimension_scores", {}))
   147→
   148→    # 3. Plan-aware ordering (part 1: separate skipped items)
   149→    new_ids, skipped = _plan_presort(items, state, plan)
   150→
   151→    # 4. Lifecycle filter — endgame-only items filtered when objective work remains
   152→    items = apply_lifecycle_filter(items)
   153→
   154→    # 5. Sort & plan post-processing
   155→    items.sort(key=item_sort_key)
   156→    _plan_postsort(items, skipped, plan, opts)
   157→
   158→    # 6. Finalize
   159→    total = len(items)
   160→    if opts.count is not None and opts.count > 0:
   161→        items = items[:opts.count]
   162→    if opts.explain:
   163→        for item in items:
   164→            item["explain"] = item_explain(item)
   165→
   166→    return {
   167→        "items": items,
   168→        "total": total,
   169→        "grouped": group_queue_items(items, "item"),
   170→        "new_ids": new_ids,
   171→    }
   172→
   173→
   174→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   175→# Pipeline helpers (private to this module)
   176→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   177→
   178→
   179→def _resolve_inputs(
   180→    opts: QueueBuildOptions, state: StateModel,
   181→) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None, str, float]:
   182→    """Resolve plan, scan_path, status, and subjective threshold from options."""
   183→    ctx = opts.context
   184→    plan = ctx.plan if ctx is not None else opts.plan
   185→
   186→    scan_path: str | None = (
   187→        state.get("scan_path")
   188→        if isinstance(opts.scan_path, _ScanPathFromState)
   189→        else opts.scan_path
   190→    )
   191→
   192→    status = opts.status
   193→    if status not in ALL_STATUSES:
   194→        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported status filter: {status}")
   195→
   196→    try:
   197→        threshold = float(opts.subjective_threshold)
   198→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
   199→        threshold = 100.0
   200→    threshold = max(0.0, min(100.0, threshold))
   201→
   202→    return plan, scan_path, status, threshold
   203→
```

1. Deferred disposition (if present) - blocks everything else
2. Post-flight scan
3. Post-flight non-objective items (subjective review)

```
   100→def _reconcile(state: dict, plan: dict, monkeypatch) -> dict:
   101→    """Simulate a scan boundary: run reconcile_plan_post_scan with mocked I/O."""
   102→    saved: list[dict] = []

   104→    monkeypatch.setattr(reconcile_mod, "save_plan", lambda p, _path=None: saved.append(p))
   105→    reconcile_mod.reconcile_plan_post_scan(SimpleNamespace(
   106→        state=state, state_path=Path("/tmp/fake-state.json"), config={},
   107→    ))
   108→    return saved[-1] if saved else plan

   111→def _queue_ids(state: dict, plan: dict) -> list[str]:
   112→    result = build_work_queue(state, options=QueueBuildOptions(plan=plan, count=None))
   113→    return [item["id"] for item in result["items"]]
```

```
    74→    return item.get("id") == WORKFLOW_DEFERRED_DISPOSITION_ID
    75→
    76→
    77→def _has_deferred_disposition(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> bool:
    78→    return any(_is_deferred_disposition(item) for item in items)
    79→
    80→
    81→def _is_postflight_scan(item: WorkQueueItem) -> bool:
    82→    return item.get("id") == WORKFLOW_RUN_SCAN_ID
    83→
    84→
    85→def _has_postflight_scan(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> bool:
    86→    return any(_is_postflight_scan(item) for item in items)
    87→
    88→
    89→def _is_triage_stage(item: WorkQueueItem) -> bool:
    90→    """True when item is a triage workflow stage."""
    91→    return (
    92→        item.get("kind") == "workflow_stage"
    93→        and str(item.get("id", "")).startswith("triage::")
    94→    )
    95→
    96→
    97→def _is_postflight_workflow(item: WorkQueueItem) -> bool:
    98→    return (
    99→        item.get("kind") == "workflow_action"
   100→        and not _is_deferred_disposition(item)
   101→        and not _is_postflight_scan(item)
   102→    )
   103→
   104→
   105→def _has_postflight_workflow(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> bool:
   106→    return any(_is_postflight_workflow(item) for item in items)
   107→
   108→
   109→def _is_force_visible(item: WorkQueueItem) -> bool:
   110→    """True when the item is explicitly escalated past objective gating."""
   111→    return bool(item.get("force_visible"))
   112→
   113→
   114→def _is_postflight_phase_item(item: WorkQueueItem) -> bool:
   115→    return (
   116→        _is_postflight_non_objective_item(item)
   117→        or _is_triage_stage(item)
   118→        or _is_deferred_disposition(item)
   119→        or _is_postflight_scan(item)
   120→        or _is_postflight_workflow(item)
   121→    )
   122→
   123→
   124→def apply_lifecycle_filter(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   125→    """Enforce lifecycle visibility rules."""
   126→    if _has_initial_reviews(items):
   127→        return [
   128→            item for item in items
   129→            if item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension" and item.get("initial_review")
   130→        ]
   131→
   132→    if _has_objective_items(items):
   133→        return [
   134→            item for item in items
   135→            if not _is_postflight_phase_item(item) or _is_force_visible(item)
   136→        ]
   137→
   138→    # Explicit post-flight sequence:
   139→    #   deferred backlog disposition -> scan -> subjective review -> workflow -> triage
   140→    if _has_deferred_disposition(items):
   141→        return [
   142→            item for item in items
   143→            if _is_deferred_disposition(item) or _is_force_visible(item)
   144→        ]
   145→    if _has_postflight_scan(items):
   146→        return [
   147→            item for item in items
   148→            if _is_postflight_scan(item) or _is_force_visible(item)
   149→        ]
   150→    if _has_postflight_non_objective_items(items):
   151→        return [
   152→            item for item in items
   153→            if _is_postflight_non_objective_item(item) or _is_force_visible(item)
   154→        ]
   155→    if _has_postflight_workflow(items):
   156→        return [
   157→            item for item in items
   158→            if _is_postflight_workflow(item) or _is_force_visible(item)
   159→        ]
   160→    if _has_triage_stages(items):
   161→        return [item for item in items if _is_triage_stage(item) or _is_force_visible(item)]
   162→    return items
   163→
   164→
   165→__all__ = ["apply_lifecycle_filter"]
   166→
```

> AGENT

The lifecycle is:
1. Initial reviews (blocks everything)
2. Objective items (filters postflight phase items — which includes workflow_action like communicate-score)
3. Deferred disposition
4. Postflight scan  
5. Postflight non-objective (review/subjective_review items)
6. Postflight workflow (communicate-score, create-plan)
7. Triage stages

So `communicate-score` IS filtered out when objective items exist. The test `test_workflow_items_injected_on_next_scan` expects both `communicate-score` AND `obj-1` in the queue simultaneously — that's now impossible with the lifecycle filter.

The test needs updating: communicate-score only becomes visible after objectives are completed.

Let me update each test:

The lifecycle sequence is: postflight_workflow (communicate-score, create-plan) comes before triage in the lifecycle. So after resolving review issues, workflow items appear before triage. Let me look at the full sequence again:

```
1. Initial reviews → block everything  
2. Objective items → filter postflight items  
3. Deferred disposition  
4. Postflight scan  
5. Postflight non-objective items (review, subjective_review, etc.)
6. Postflight workflow (communicate-score, create-plan)  
7. Triage stages  
```

So triage only unlocks after workflow items are completed. Let me update:
